doc.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023

title: 'Runaway Soul' and the push and pull of joy and pain
summary: She explains the blue night behind 'Runaway Soul', an uptempo shuffle whose lyrics say more than an ordinary blues.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’d like to read — one of my favorites of yours, “Runaway Soul” — and it says, “I believe my soul has found a happy home/Left me here to suffer on my own.” When I look at your song titles and your lyrics I see a lot of instances of this sort of push and pull between joy and pain, and that particular line has so much in it. Do you remember toiling over that line?

I do. I remember that particular night just having a really rough night. I call it, when you get blue, I got blue. And it’s funny people listen to that song and they think it’s about being very up, but it really is what you caught on to, very push/pull. And it was one of those songs that just kind of wrote itself and I just remember having a hard time. I don’t know if it was about a relationship, which is where I was in my life, but I just was having a really, really blue — not necessarily a dark night — but it was — I needed to just think about where I was and I felt like I was feeling — I felt very much alone but I know that there’s somebody out there, there’s something out there that’s working its way to me. Meanwhile I’m going to do my best to just hold on and stay open and leave room for that, which is probably why it ended up being an uptempo blues song, really kind of a
push/pull. It’s a shuffle but if you’re really listening to the lyrics they say a lot more than your ordinary blues song. Thank you for catching that.
Oh when you said, [sings] “Somebody help me” oh my God. There’s nothing like a good shuffle in my opinion.
Yeah. That’s when I went Gospeling, you know started blues and just kind of — somebody help me. Woo. Yeah just reach out, reach out, somebody reach out. I’ll reach out just grab my hand.
